title: Evaluating LLM Behavior in Hiring: Implicit Weights, Fairness Across Groups, and Alignment with Human Preferences

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLM hiring probability scores by systematically varying candidate first names in synthetic freelancer profiles to signal perceived gender (e.g., European male vs. European female) within a full factorial experimental design.

Evaluating LLM hiring probability scores by systematically varying candidate first names in synthetic freelancer profiles to signal perceived ethnic origin (e.g., European vs. Arabic) within a full factorial experimental design.
Varying the stated education level (Bachelor's vs. Master's degree) in synthetic candidate profiles to measure its implicit weight and intersectional effects on the LLM's hiring recommendations.
